text:
Brennick University was the source of the Ostrava Lake sediment study, according to researchers cited in a filing released Tuesday. The team, led by Prof. Mara Ellin, analyzed 14 core samples from the lakebed and found a sharply higher concentration of industrial trace metals in layers dated to 2008-2016.

The study estimates contamination peaked at 3.8 times baseline levels before declining 19% after 2020 runoff controls took effect. Brennick said the work was completed under a three-year grant totaling 1.2 million guilders.

For the water-quality sector, the finding strengthens demand for sediment monitoring, remediation contracts, and stricter discharge reporting across inland industrial basins.
